definition: Studying or computationally modeling how humans learn language — or how models acquire linguistic structure from data.
details: Studying or computationally modeling how humans learn language — or how models acquire linguistic structure from data. In NLP it motivates probing what neural models learn without explicit grammar.

explainer.lead: Language acquisition covers both how humans learn language and how models pick up linguistic structure from data. It matters because it frames what a model learns without being given an explicit grammar.

tiers.eli5: It's the question of how you learned to talk just from hearing people — and whether a machine learning from text does something similar.
tiers.practitioner: In NLP it motivates probing what neural models learn when no grammar is supplied. The pitfall is reading human-like structure into behaviour that may arise from surface statistics.
tiers.paperLevel: Studying or computationally modeling how humans learn language — or how models acquire linguistic structure from data; in NLP it motivates probing what neural models learn without explicit grammar.

explainer.example: Researchers probe a trained model to see what linguistic structure it acquired purely from data.
